stage1.impression: A dim, warm back-bar with lit shelves of bottles either side of a niche holding a clear box speaker. It reads as a tidy real-time or game render, not a photograph. The bottles are a few cloned models with identical labels. The concrete is a soft blotchy texture with no formwork, and the counter is a featureless brown smear. The speaker sits against a flat, cool grey panel that makes it look like a fish tank or a vending display, not the hero. There is no sign of life in the foreground, and a pendant is cut in half at the frame edge.

blocking_9: The speaker must read at a glance as a thick, polished cast-acrylic horn cabinet, with glowing edges and the horn's form visible through the clear. At present it reads as a smoky box in front of a grey panel.
The niche's frosted back must sit warm and in the room's palette, with the glow falling off. It must not be a flat cool-grey rectangle (now 89/84/85 RGB, lum range only 68 across it).
No repeated bottle models or labels. The back-bar needs varied heights, glass colours, label designs and fill levels.
The concrete must show board-form grain, tie holes and pour lines at 1:1, and the fir counter must show grain, sheen and a pool of pendant light.
A foreground sign of life (the card's 'glass near'), in the bottom third and in focus or gently soft.
The pendant must be fully in frame or deliberately out of it. Now it is a half tube clipped at x 680-720 with 0.8 % clipping.
Delivered at full resolution (2400 x 1600) with no denoiser smear on the labels or the speaker's internals.

defects.what: Bottles are clones: the same three or four shapes with identical cream-and-red labels repeat on every shelf.
The same bottle clones repeat on the right shelves.
The niche back is a flat cool-grey panel (RGB 89/84/85, delta E 35 from a warm 2600 K frosted glow). It is the only cool surface in the frame and reads as a blank screen.
The upper cabinet and horn read as a smoky blob behind a thin rounded-rect outline. No thickness, no glowing polished edges. The horn's silhouette is muddy and doubled by refraction.
The white batts and woofer area is the brightest thing on the speaker (median 101, p95 197) and reads as a white appliance or washing-machine door, not batts behind clear.
The shelves' lit edges are hard, uniform white lines (p95 about 200 against a background of about 20). They read as LED strip signage, and they are almost as bright as the pendant.
The concrete above the niche is a flat, blotchy procedural texture (lum range 17.6). No formwork boards, tie holes or pour lines.
The fir counter is a smeared dark brown with no grain, no reflection of the bottles or the pendant, and no pool of light. The bottom-left falls to lum about 10.
The pendant is cut by the frame edge, and its frosted tube clips (0.8 %). It is a distracting bright bar at the edge.
No glass, menu or hand in the foreground, although the card lists a glass near. The scene feels like an empty set.
Proof at 720 x 480 shows denoiser softness on the labels and the speaker's interior. Verticals are true and the lens is believable.

changes.problem: The niche's frosted back is cool grey and flat, so the speaker is silhouetted against a blank panel instead of glowing with warm light through its clear acrylic.

evidence.measured: RGB median 89/84/85, delta E 35.4 against #B8A888, lum range 67.6; the rest of the frame is r>g>b warm (for example 36/24/14)

change.setting: niches' frosted backs emission strength and colour, plus the niche spots
change.from: 0.12, effectively neutral; spots 2 x 220 W 2600 K cone 20
change.to: 0.06 at 2400 K tint, with a vertical gradient (brighter at the bottom behind the batts, falling off towards the top). Niche spots 2 x 160 W 2600 K, cone 30 deg, aimed to graze the cabinet's side edges rather than flood the back

changes.expected: The back becomes a warm, soft glow that falls off upwards, and the cabinet's edges catch light and outline its thickness.

changes.problem: The back-bar bottles are a few cloned models with identical labels, which is the clearest 'render' tell in the frame.

evidence.measured: Seen at 3x: the same cream label with red bands repeats on more than 15 bottles, from 3 to 4 silhouettes

change.from: a few repeated models, one label design
change.to: at least 12 distinct bottle models (squat, tall, decanter, amaro, Japanese whisky, mezcal), clear, amber and green-black glass, varied fill levels, at least 8 label designs, mostly dark or kraft labels so that few labels are bright cream. Leave some gaps and lean two bottles slightly forward

changes.expected: The shelves read as a working bar's stock, with small specular highlights on varied glass and no bright repeated label pattern.

changes.problem: The shelves' lit edges are hard white lines, nearly as bright as the pendant, and read as LED strip signage instead of glowing polished acrylic edges.

evidence.measured: p95 200.7 against a median of 31.4; the same holds for the shelves at y 85-100 and on the right at y 145-165

change.to: 0.35, warmed to 2400 K. Make the shelves read 25 mm thick, with a slight bevel on the polished front edge so the glow has depth

changes.expected: The edges glow amber and soft and become secondary to the speaker. The bottles are lit from beneath without white bars across the frame.

changes.problem: Nothing in the foreground shows the room is in use, and the card's 'glass near' is not visible.

evidence.measured: Only the empty counter; lum median 28

change.setting: props: rocks glass and folded menu on the counter
change.to: a heavy rocks glass with a large ice cube and a finger of whisky at about x 180-280, y 360-480 of the frame, catching the pendant, slightly soft at f/4. Add a folded menu edge and a candle in an amber votive at lower right

changes.expected: Foreground depth and life, a warm specular on the glass, and the counter gains a pool of light.

changes.problem: The fir counter reads as smeared brown with no grain, sheen or light pool.

evidence.measured: Lum median 28, p5 9.4; the x-profile runs 10.6 to 52 to 26.9 with no texture

change.setting: the fir's stain and finish, plus the pendant aim
change.to: a medium-honey oiled finish, roughness 0.35, with a visible quarter-sawn grain normal map at the real scale. Aim one pendant spot (180 W 2400 K) so that its pool lands on the counter between the glass and the niche

changes.expected: A readable pool of light on the counter with grain and a soft reflection of the speaker and bottles, and the bottom-left lifted.

changes.problem: The pendant is cut in half at the right edge and clips, pulling the eye away from the speaker.

evidence.measured: Median 191.9, clip 0.8 %; only half the tube is in frame

change.to: pan about 2 deg to the right so the pendant sits fully in the top-right third, or about 3 deg to the left to drop it out entirely. Lower the pendant tube emission from 0.25 to 0.15

changes.expected: The pendant becomes a complete practical that reads as a lamp, or disappears. The speaker remains centred.

changes.problem: The concrete is a flat blotchy procedural texture without board-form evidence.

evidence.measured: Lum range 17.6, median 25.6, no linear structure at 3x

change.to: board-formed texture with 150 mm horizontal boards, 2 tie holes per panel at 600 mm centres, a faint pour line, roughness 0.8 with a slight sheen. Add a grazing sconce or the niche spill so the texture shows

changes.expected: The wall reads as cast concrete with visible lines, and luminance varies along the boards.

changes.problem: The batts and woofer area outshines the rest of the speaker and reads as a white appliance instead of batts glimpsed through thick clear acrylic.

evidence.measured: Median 101.2, p95 197.1, against the upper cabinet median of 64.2

change.from: 2 x 220 W spots flooding the lower cabinet, exposure 1.45
change.to: aim the spots at the cabinet's top and side edges, cone 30. Exposure 1.3 so the batts sit at about 70-85 and the polished acrylic edges carry the highlights

changes.expected: The speaker reads as one object top to bottom with glowing edges. The batts become a soft white behind the clear.

out_of_scope.request: Make the Fog cabinet's acrylic visibly thicker, or tint it so the speaker carries the frame's colour.
out_of_scope.why: The speaker's shape, colour and parts are fixed. The Fog pair is water-clear by design, so this frame has no saturated hero colour. Consider featuring an Ember speaker if the owner wants colour here.

out_of_scope.request: Replace the flat rounded-rect form of the upper cabinet so the horn reads more clearly.
